intro: You've searched for a landlord tax advisor near you, which usually means you own rental property and want someone local who understands the tax side of being a landlord. Whether it's income tax on rent, capital gains when you sell, or how to hold property with others, a specialist can help you see the options clearly. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK tax adviser who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a landlord tax advisor near me usually need
need_lead: Most landlords looking for a local tax adviser want practical help with the tax consequences of owning and letting property.
needs: You rent out a flat or house and want to understand how income tax applies to your rental profit, including what expenses you can deduct.
You are thinking about buying or selling a residential property and need to know about capital gains tax and how quickly a gain must be reported.
You own property jointly with a spouse, partner or friend and wonder whether the way you hold it affects how tax is worked out.
You are considering transferring property into a company and want to know whether incorporation is right for your situation.
You have several properties and want a clear overview of the income tax, capital gains and inheritance tax issues across your portfolio.
context_heading: One key thing to understand about landlord tax advice
context: Tax adviser is not a protected title in the UK, so anyone can call themselves one. The main specialist bodies are the Chartered Institute of Taxation and the Association of Taxation Technicians, and their members follow a shared code called Professional Conduct in Relation to Taxation. Many accountants and solicitors also advise on tax.

Tax advisers who charge a fee must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, and HMRC has been tightening standards for paid tax agents. It is sensible to ask about qualifications, supervision and professional indemnity insurance before you go ahead. iComply is not regulated and does not give tax advice itself; we simply introduce you to a professional who can.

tell: Mention that you searched for a landlord tax advisor near me and say where you are based, so we can introduce you to someone suitable for your area.
Describe the property or properties you own, including whether they are let out, and how they are currently owned.
Explain what you want help with, such as income tax on rent, capital gains when selling, inheritance tax planning, or whether to incorporate.

questions: What qualifications and professional body memberships do you hold for tax advice?

faqs.q: Do I need a specialist landlord tax adviser or can my usual accountant help?
faqs.a: Many accountants advise on landlord tax, and some tax advisers specialise in property. It is reasonable to ask about their experience with rental income, capital gains and ownership structures before you decide.

faqs.q: What does 'near me' mean for tax advice – do I need to meet in person?
faqs.a: Tax advice can often be given remotely, but some landlords prefer a local adviser they can meet. Tell iComply your preference and we will introduce you to a suitable professional.

faqs.q: Is incorporation always the best way to hold rental property?
faqs.a: No, incorporation is not right for everyone. A tax adviser can look at your personal circumstances and explain the pros and cons of owning property personally or through a company.

faqs.q: How are gains on residential property reported?
faqs.a: Gains on residential property must be reported quickly, and there are deadlines for both reporting and paying any tax due. A tax adviser can tell you the exact rules that apply to your sale.

extra_heading: What happens at a first meeting with a local landlord tax adviser
extra: A first meeting with a landlord tax adviser is mostly a fact-finding conversation. Expect questions about every property you own, how each one is held, the rent it brings in, any mortgages on it, and what you plan to do with it next. Bring the paperwork you already have, such as tenancy agreements, mortgage statements and recent tax returns, so the adviser can see the real picture rather than a rough one.

The adviser will then talk you through how the rules apply to your situation, covering income tax on rental profit, capital gains when a property is sold, and inheritance tax if your portfolio is large enough to bring it into play. If you hold property jointly, they may explain how the way you own it affects how tax is worked out. They may also discuss whether incorporation could suit you, while being clear that it is not right for everyone.

Before the meeting ends, ask how they charge and whether you will get a written quote, since fees are on application and vary between practices. It is also worth asking who will actually handle your work and how they prefer to be contacted. iComply is not regulated and does not give tax advice; we simply introduce you to a professional who can.

extra_faqs.q: I already have an accountant – is it worth seeing a landlord tax adviser as well?
extra_faqs.a: It can be, especially if your accountant deals mainly with your rental accounts and you want help with capital gains, inheritance tax or ownership structures across a portfolio. Some landlords use a specialist for one-off decisions while keeping their accountant for the annual return. Ask both how they would work together so nothing is duplicated.

extra_faqs.q: Can a landlord tax adviser help if I only own one property?
extra_faqs.a: Yes. A single rental flat or house still raises questions about deductible expenses, joint ownership and what happens if you sell. A short conversation can be enough to set things straight before a decision is made.
